module_title: Parliament: Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha - Basic Understanding
introduction: The Parliament is the supreme legislative (law-making) body of India. According to Article 79 of the Constitution, the Parliament of India consists of three parts: The President, the Rajya Sabha (Upper House), and the Lok Sabha (Lower House). India follows a bicameral (two-house) system.

core_concepts.title: Lok Sabha (House of the People)
core_concepts.description: It is the Lower House. Members are directly elected by the public. Its normal term is 5 years. The maximum strength is 550 (earlier 552, but the 2 Anglo-Indian nominated seats were abolished by the 104th Amendment Act). The minimum age to become an MP is 25 years.

core_concepts.title: Rajya Sabha (Council of States)
core_concepts.description: It is the Upper House. Members are indirectly elected by MLAs of the states. It is a permanent body and cannot be dissolved. Its maximum strength is 250 (238 elected + 12 nominated by the President). The minimum age is 30 years.

core_concepts.title: Tenure of Members
core_concepts.description: A Lok Sabha MP serves a term of 5 years (unless the house is dissolved earlier). A Rajya Sabha MP serves a term of 6 years, with one-third (1/3rd) of its members retiring every 2 years.

core_concepts.title: Presiding Officers
core_concepts.description: The Lok Sabha is headed by the 'Speaker' (elected by Lok Sabha members). The Rajya Sabha is headed by the 'Chairman'. The Vice-President of India acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

important_entities.name: The President of India
important_entities.significance: Even though the President does not sit in either House, no bill passed by Parliament can become a law without their assent (signature).

important_entities.name: G.V. Mavalankar
important_entities.significance: He is often referred to as the 'Father of the Lok Sabha'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: No. A common mistake is thinking the President is a member of Parliament. The President is an 'integral part' of Parliament but NOT a member of either House.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Term of Rajya Sabha vs. Term of its Members
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a question asks 'What is the term of the Rajya Sabha?', the answer is 'Permanent' (It has no term). If it asks 'What is the term of a Rajya Sabha member?', the answer is '6 years'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.trick_title: Articles for Parliament, RS, and LS
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Sa = Sansad/Parliament (Article 79), Ra = Rajya Sabha (Article 80), La = Lok Sabha (Article 81).

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize the minimum age requirements: President/VP/Governor = 35, Rajya Sabha/MLC = 30, Lok Sabha/MLA = 25, Panchayat = 21.
Remember that the President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha from fields of Art, Literature, Science, and Social Service.
